facts.text: Articulated steering turns a machine by bending it at a hinge between its front and rear halves; this suits rough ground but makes the machine swing and pitch during braking.
facts.quote: Articulated steering turns a machine by bending it at a hinge between its front and rear halves, which suits rough ground but makes the machine swing and pitch when it brakes.

facts.text: During braking while turning, on a side slope or at a large articulation angle, an articulated machine's halves push against each other through the hinge, potentially causing sideways motion of the front (yaw), body lean (roll), axle load transfer and changes in hinge angle.
facts.quote: the two halves push on each other through the hinge: the front may be pushed sideways (yaw), the body may lean (roll), load moves between the axles, and the hinge angle itself can change.

facts.text: Academic models of articulated wheel loaders with 7 and 8 degrees of freedom treat roll instability as the critical mode.
facts.quote: academic models of articulated wheel loaders with 7 and 8 degrees of freedom treat roll instability as the critical mode

facts.text: Academic models of articulated wheel loaders with 7 and 8 degrees of freedom were validated on scaled models.
facts.quote: academic models of articulated wheel loaders with 7 and 8 degrees of freedom treat roll instability as the critical mode and were validated on scaled models

facts.text: Published data on jackknife or roll events during automatic braking of articulated off-road machines were not found.
facts.quote: published data on jackknife or roll events during automatic braking of articulated off-road machines were not found [Chapter 8]

facts.text: ISO/PRF 21815-5 treats articulation as a distinct collision-relevant motion and distinguishes stationary articulation, in which the rear swings without machine travel, from ordinary steering during travel.
facts.quote: ISO/PRF 21815-5 treats articulation as its own collision-relevant motion and distinguishes articulation of a stationary machine, where the rear swings although the machine is not traveling, from ordinary steering during travel

facts.text: Stability of articulated machines and machines with a high center of gravity during hard braking is one of four areas identified by the booklet where a point-mass model is insufficient and a multibody model is needed.
facts.quote: Articulated and high-center-of-gravity stability during hard braking is one of the four places where the booklet says a point-mass model is not enough and a multibody model is needed

facts.text: The deceleration commanded by an automatic brake must be capped according to the machine's articulation and roll state.
facts.quote: the deceleration the automatic brake may command has to be capped by the articulation and roll state [Chapter 8]

facts.text: The booklet's test matrix includes stops at the articulation limit and on a side slope for articulated machines.
facts.quote: The test matrix therefore includes stops at the articulation limit and on a side slope for articulated machines [Chapter 8].
